statement: The Byzantine-Ostrogothic conflict (535–554) — Justinian I's reconquest of Italy from the Ostrogothic Kingdom — was the most destructive war in Italian history. General Belisarius captured Sicily (535), Naples (536), and Rome (536) in a rapid advance, then General Narses completed the conquest after the Gothic King Totila's recovery and recapture of Rome (546, 550). The war lasted 20 years, killing or displacing perhaps a third of Italy's population, destroying the senatorial aristocracy, and collapsing urban life throughout the peninsula. The Lombard invasion followed 14 years after the war ended, exploiting Byzantine exhaustion.
